correctness.rationale: For all integer n>=3 and t>0, cyclic averaging by concavity reduces attainment to a two-weight sunlet. Fourier diagonalization yields the exact Fiedler value h(a,b,mu)=a+mu*b/2-sqrt(a^2+(mu*b/2)^2) with mu=4*sin(pi/n)^2. The product identity (a-r)*(mu*b/2-r)=r^2/2 and sharp weighted AM-GM yield the claimed budget bound, explicit positive equality weights, and uniqueness within the symmetric class. Equality of both first-harmonic Rayleigh quotients transfers through the averaging argument to arbitrary optimal allocations, forcing every pendant weight, then every cycle weight, to its symmetric value by a nonzero planar chord determinant. The t>0 and n>=3 boundary assumptions are used. The n->infinity laws follow from mu~4*pi^2/n^2; they are analytical, not inferred from finite tests. A stand-alone checker executed successfully: 168 exact-rational identities, 36 full-Laplacian eigenspectra, and 1080 nonsymmetric feasible comparisons.

originality.rationale: The reviewed early works contain general semidefinite and embedding frameworks for maximizing algebraic connectivity and examples for trees and plain cycles. The 2008 structural work mainly treats trees and graph-level necessary/sufficient optimality conditions; the 2022 fixed weighted-corona results concern normalized/signless spectra and Kirchhoff indices. Those ingredients do not explicitly give the price-dependent ordinary-Laplacian optimum for sunlets or the rigidity proof against all asymmetric allocations. Indexed specialized queries and nearby published results identified no equivalent statement. Residual risk remains for unindexed or uninspected historical specializations; passing this search-based self-review is not proof of worldwide novelty. A further full-text check of Du et al. (2022) found a fixed-weight ordinary-Laplacian polynomial and coherence formulas, but no priced spectral-gap optimal design.
residual_risks: An equivalent theorem could exist in unindexed older graph-optimization literature or a historical thesis; web and semantic search are not completeness guarantees.
Some papers were inspected through indexed HTML extraction rather than every figure in an original PDF; no uninspected plausible item established stronger covering implications.
Self-review and finite checker results are not independent mathematical validation.

value.rationale: A sunlet models a ring backbone with one terminal at each station. The sharp rule allocates money simultaneously to backbone and terminal conductances for arbitrary positive relative price and any ring size, proving that both edge classes remain essential at the global optimum and that no hidden asymmetric alternative attains the gap. The exact formula exposes a nontrivial scale separation between individual pendant and cycle conductances and a t~n^2 price-size crossover, quantities a generic SDP solver or fixed-spectrum table does not itself report. This is a complete natural infinite-family optimization with exact and motivated parameters, not an isolated tiny numerical gain or terminology change.
